songInfo.title: Patience
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

keyAndScale.primaryKey: G major (sounding F# major tuned down half-step)

scalesUsed.notes: G - A - B - C - D - E - F# - G
scalesUsed.application: Underpins the foundational open acoustic chord voicings (C, G, D, Em)

scalesUsed.notes: A - B - C# - D - E - F# - G# - A
scalesUsed.application: Introduces the C# note in the major II chord (A), creating the song's signature romantic pull
Drives Slash's melodic acoustic intro fills, whistling hooks, and solo embellishments

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Ionian with major II secondary dominant tension and soulful acoustic rock swagger
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: E minor is the relative minor of G major

mainProgression.description: The unforgettable verse progression in G major. Incorporating the non-diatonic major II chord (A major instead of Am) introduces a C# note acting as a secondary dominant (V of V) pushing forcefully into D.

sectionProgressions.progression: C - G - A - D - C - G - A - D
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: IV - I - II - V - IV - I - II - V
sectionProgressions.description: Intimate arpeggiated acoustic picking under the legendary whistling melody and soulful verse lyrics

sectionProgressions.progression: C - G - C - Em - C - G - D
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: IV - I - IV - vi - IV - I - V
sectionProgressions.description: The emotional chorus balancing the warmth of C and G against the dark melancholy of E minor

sectionProgressions.progression: D - G - D - G - D - G
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: V - I - V - I - V - I
sectionProgressions.description: The dynamic acoustic explosion cycling between D and G with full strumming and passionate vocal chants
Open G major and A mixolydian scale study demonstrating lead acoustic embellishments around cowboy chord shapes

harmonicFunction: C (IV) - Subdominant chord establishing the floating, hopeful beginning of each phrase
G (I) - Tonic chord offering sweet, momentary grounding
A (II) - Major second secondary dominant (V/V) containing C# that builds strong romantic tension
D (V) - Dominant chord resolving the phrase and setting up the next cycle
Em (vi) - Relative minor providing dramatic weight during the chorus

techniques.name: Arpeggiated Acoustic Flatpicking & Embellishments
techniques.description: Individual note picking across chord shapes combined with signature hammer-ons and suspensions (such as D to Dsus4 to Dsus2)

notes: C chord: Hammer index finger on the B string (fret 1) or middle finger on D string (fret 2)
G chord: Pick root on string 6, then arpeggiate through strings 4, 3, and 2
A chord: Standard open A with open high E ringing
D chord: Hammer-on pinky on 1st string 3rd fret for Dsus4, release to high E for Dsus2
sequence: Pick the root bass note cleanly on beat 1
Arpeggiate upward through the middle strings
Execute the melodic hammer-on on beat 3 or 4
Move smoothly to the next chord shape without dropping the tempo
tips: Hold the chord shape down firmly with your fretting hand so notes ring into each other
Keep your picking wrist light and floating above the soundhole
Practice the D - Dsus4 - D - Dsus2 embellishment slowly until it flows naturally

techniques.name: Dynamic Strumming Crescendo
techniques.description: Building from delicate, quiet acoustic fingerpicking in the intro to full, room-filling downstroke strumming during the anthemic outro

notes: Verse: Gentle arpeggios and light brushes
Chorus: Steady 8th-note strumming
Outro: Heavy downstroke power strums on D and G with full right-hand commitment
sequence: Maintain quiet acoustic intimacy through the first two verses
Open up your strumming arm during the chorus
When the tempo accelerates and the band enters the outro, dig in with aggressive, full downstrokes
Let all 6 strings ring out with maximum dreadnought acoustic volume
tips: Use a flexible medium pick (0.60mm to 0.73mm) so aggressive strumming does not sound harsh
Lock into the backbeat accents on beats 2 and 4
The outro is one of the most celebrated sing-alongs in rock history — play it with total confidence

sections.name: Intro Riff & Whistling
sections.description: Slash, Izzy, and Duff open on three acoustic guitars with delicate arpeggios and suspensions under Axl Rose's legendary whistling motif.
notes: Guitars tuned down a half-step: Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb
Pick individual strings cleanly inside each cowboy chord shape
Add the pinky suspension on the D chord (Dsus4 on fret 3 string 1)
Keep the rhythm intimate and swaying at 88 BPM

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Axl delivers the gentle, romantic verses over the C - G - A - D progression with delicate acoustic support.
notes: Notice the emotional lift when moving to the A major chord
Let the open strings chime together like a harp
Maintain relaxed wrist motion at 88 BPM

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The chorus opens with a fuller strum, introducing the dark Em chord before resolving through G and D.
sections.progression: C - G - C - Em - C - G - D
notes: Strum with broader dynamic strokes
Emphasize the emotional turn into the Em chord
Ramp up intensity into the next section
sections.exerciseLabel: Acoustic Chorus Flow with Em Dip

sections.name: Outro Singalong
sections.description: The legendary campfire finale: cycling continuously between D and G with full-throttle acoustic strumming as Axl belts the famous outro.
sections.progression: D - G - D - G - D - G
notes: Explode into maximum dynamic strumming volume
Hard downstroke accents driving the two-chord rock turnaround
Encourage everyone around the campfire to join in on the harmony vocals
sections.exerciseLabel: All We Need Is Just a Little Patience Outro

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.description: Scale run demonstrating the C# chromatic alteration over the A major chord inside the open G framework.
notes: Notice the difference between the natural C on string 2 fret 1 and the C# on string 2 fret 2
Alternate picking across strings 6 to 1
Sustain the tonic G note with controlled vibrato
sections.exerciseLabel: G Major with Secondary Dominant Scale Exercise

guitar.recommended: Guild Songbird or Gibson J-200 / Hummingbird Acoustic
alternatives: Any 6-string acoustic guitar tuned down a half-step
guitar.pickup: Under-saddle acoustic pickup or natural microphone capture

amp.recommended: Clean acoustic amplifier or direct to mixing console

effects.reverb: Subtle studio hall reverb for acoustic depth
effects.other: Medium pick (0.60mm to 0.73mm) for balanced flatpicking articulation

beginner.title: Master the Outro & Cowboy Chords
steps: Tune your guitar down a half-step: Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb (or play along in standard)
Learn open C, G, A, and D chord shapes cleanly
Practice the dynamic outro (D to G) with energetic downstroke strumming
Play along with the outro chant at 88 BPM

intermediate.title: Nail the Arpeggiated Picking & Dsus Embellishments
steps: Practice the fingerpicking pattern: pick the bass root followed by three treble strings
Add the Dsus4 (pinky on fret 3 high E string) and Dsus2 (open high E) embellishments
Work on smooth chord transitions between C and G, then A and D
Play through the verse and chorus sections with a metronome at 88 BPM

advanced.title: Full Acoustic Arrangement with Slash's Fills
steps: Learn Slash's acoustic lead fills and double-stop licks between vocal phrases
Master the dynamic transition into the driving outro with full strumming authority
Whistle or sing lead vocals while maintaining the intricate picking groove
Perform the full 6-minute acoustic masterpiece from memory

commonMistakes: Playing in standard tuning along with the original record — remember GN'R is tuned down a half-step
Muting the high E string on the A major chord — arch your fingers so it rings open
Rushing through the Dsus4 embellishments instead of keeping them melodic and rhythmic
Losing tempo momentum when transitioning from the chorus into the outro
practiceRoutine: 2 minutes: Half-step down tuning verification across all 6 strings
5 minutes: Arpeggiated picking on C, G, A, and D with metronome at 80 BPM
5 minutes: D to Dsus4 to Dsus2 suspension drill
5 minutes: Chorus flow including the quick transition into Em
5 minutes: Energetic run-through of the D - G outro strumming pattern
focusAreas: Crisp pinky coordination on the Dsus4 suspension
Dynamic acoustic build into the outro
metronomeWork: Start at 75 BPM to lock in the arpeggiated picking pattern
Gradually increase to 88 BPM for authentic GN'R groove
Practice with clicks on beats 2 and 4 to internalize relaxed rock timekeeping
Ensure steady tempo during the transition into the energetic outro
